items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Freddie Johnson was one that -- the pianist who I worked with Sapiro's band

ctx.x: Yeah, who liked it so much, because you know, -- for a lot of reasons. You know, because there wasn't -- things weren't segregated over there like they were over here, and they got -- there was more freedom of action, freedom of playing, and you could -- so there were a whole lot of musicians who just stayed and lived over there and raised families and whatever. You know, which was good for them, I suppose. Freddie Johnson was one that -- the pianist who I worked with Sapiro's band, he went over there and lived,…
when the war broke out he was even in a concentration camp.
